questions.question: Which query class does a KV store handle best?
options: Semantic similarity over long conversations
Reachability across customers sharing a billing entity
Temporal queries about what was true at a past time
Direct fact lookup keyed by (user, type, entity)
questions.explanation: KV is O(1) on exact keys; vector is for similarity, graph is for relationships.

questions.question: What are the three stores Mem0 writes in parallel on each add()?
options: Vector, KV, and graph stores
Cache, queue, and log stores
Postgres, Redis, and ClickHouse
Embedding, attention, and FFN layers
questions.explanation: Mem0 fans every write out to vector, KV, and graph stores.

questions.question: What three dimensions feed Mem0's fusion score?
options: Precision, recall, and F1 score
Relevance, importance, and recency
Latency, throughput, and dollar cost
Confidence, perplexity, and BLEU score
questions.explanation: Score is a weighted sum of relevance, importance, and recency; weights tune per product.

questions.question: What does Mem0g do when an incoming fact contradicts an existing edge?
options: Raises an exception and aborts the write until a human resolves the conflict
Rewrites the user_id on the edge to match the incoming fact's source
Marks the existing edge invalid but does not delete it, so temporal queries can still traverse
Deletes the edge immediately, so no record of the earlier fact remains for temporal queries to traverse
questions.explanation: Soft invalidation preserves history for temporal (valid-at-time) queries.

questions.question: Why does the lesson recommend tuning fusion weights per product?
options: Vector libraries reject fusion scores that mix cosine similarity with non-normalized signals
The Apache 2.0 license requires every deployment to expose configurable scoring weights
Every product should use equal fixed weights across relevance, importance, and recency so retrieval stays unbiased across every use case
Recency dominates for chat agents while importance dominates for compliance agents and relevance dominates for retrieval agents
questions.explanation: Different products want different bias on relevance/importance/recency; one set of weights does not fit all.

questions.question: What is the scope taxonomy Mem0 uses?
options: User, session, and agent scope
Public, private, and secret scope
Local, regional, and global scope
Read, write, and admin scope
questions.explanation: Scopes are user (cross-session), session (one thread), agent (per-instance state).

questions.question: What is embedding drift in this pattern, and how does the lesson recommend mitigating it?
options: Vectors get encrypted at rest by default, so periodic key rotation is what keeps retrieval accurate
Vector retrieval quality degrades as the corpus grows; periodically re-embed the top-N most used records
Embeddings silently overflow their integer range as the corpus grows, so the fix is switching to float64 storage
The embedding API's URL changes between provider versions, so pinning a fixed domain keeps retrieval stable
questions.explanation: Periodic re-embedding of hot records keeps retrieval quality steady as the corpus grows.
